overclaims: A December 2025 Carnegie Mellon benchmark of coding agents on real-world tasks found the best setup's solutions were 61% functionally correct but only 10.5% secure.
The main studies are a vendor report and a preprint (later accepted at ICML 2026).
checks.note: The evidence identifies SWE-Agent with Claude 4 Sonnet, but does not establish it as the best setup or document ICML acceptance. The payload also omits that SusVibes selected tasks that had led human programmers to vulnerable implementations, a material qualification on its security rates.

overclaims: A December 2025 agent benchmark found that only 10.5% of solutions were secure, even though 61% worked.
The security evidence comes from test tasks: a vendor report and a preprint later accepted at ICML 2026.
Agent-written code that passes functional tests is mostly insecure on real-world tasks.
checks.note: ICML acceptance is unsupported. The rationale presents one agent/model configuration's rates as benchmark-wide results; the evidence excerpt names the configuration. The payload omits SusVibes' selection of tasks that had led humans to vulnerable implementations, and its evidence explanation generalizes beyond that sample.
